blocks.text: 要点

inlines.text: 要点
列出某个模型的版本，也必须能运行它。
报告的是一个 Codex 版本、实际运行的却是另一个，只会把故障从选择器挪到第一条消息。
能力信息要从列表里读，而不是从名字里猜。
服务商的列表本来就写明了某个模型支持哪些思考级别和端点。靠模型名字推断的规则，遇到第一个没见过的模型就会失效。
保留上一份可用的列表。
刷新失败或切换目录，都不该让选择器里的模型比之前更少。
一个来源出问题，不该拖累其他来源。
models.dev 上一个改了名的服务商曾让所有服务商的目录更新全部停摆，直到我们把它降级为警告。

blocks.text: How it broke

blocks.text: On September 21, models.dev split its kimi-for-coding entry into two new ones. Our publisher treated one missing provider as a fatal error, so every run failed. blocks.text: The catalog knows what exists in public. Your account knows what you can use. When you sign in to a provider, OpenClaw asks it for your model list and shows every chat model on it, including models newer than your install or models only your account can access.

inlines.text: 3. The Codex version problem

blocks.text: This is the Sol bug from the top of the post. ChatGPT decides which models to offer from the Codex version the client reports. An old version gets a shorter list.

blocks.text: Our first fix was simple. Ask npm for the latest Codex version and report that number when we fetch the list. Sol appeared in the picker.

inlines.text: Our first fix was simple. Ask npm for the latest Codex version and report that number when we fetch the list. Sol appeared in the picker.

blocks.text: A mistake we learned from

inlines.text: A mistake we learned from

blocks.text: Unfortunately, the list request said 0.161.0, but turns still ran on the bundled 0.160.0, and that binary reports its own version with every request. A model that needed anything newer would appear in the picker and then fail with HTTP 400. We had moved the failure from the picker to the first message, which is worse. We reverted it.

Now: the list and the turns use the same binary, your newest Codex, so the model is listed and runs.

blocks.text: Key takeaways

inlines.text: Key takeaways
The version that lists a model must also run it.
Reporting one Codex version and running another only moved the failure from the picker to the first message.
Read capabilities from the listing, not the name.
Provider listings already say which thinking levels and endpoints a model supports. Rules based on the model name break on the first model we have never seen.
Keep the last good list.
A failed refresh or a catalog switch should never leave the picker with fewer models than before.
One broken source should not block the rest.
A renamed provider on models.dev stopped catalog updates for every provider until we made it a warning.

blocks.text: What still needs a release

inlines.text: What still needs a release
If you have no newer Codex installed, the bundled version still decides which ChatGPT models you see.
A model newer than the catalog has no price yet. OpenClaw shows its cost as unknown, and it runs with cautious default limits until the catalog catches up.
